frequency_question: How often do major energy permitting reform bills that achieve substantive passage successfully meet specific statutory criteria for pipeline approvals without technical wording failures?
membership_rule: Members are major energy/permitting bills that passed Congress and were signed into law; excluded are bills that failed to pass or addressed unrelated sectors.

cases.name: Energy Independence and Security Act of 2007

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 4 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 4 named major packages; comprehensive energy permitting provisions when enacted uniformly satisfy standard drafting criteria for infrastructure approval.
known_gaps: Subtle ambiguities in judicial review limitations could theoretically fail strict criteria, but historically drafting matches intent.
skeleton: Total major energy/infrastructure bills enacted with permitting text divided by those meeting exact statutory criteria wording
multiplier: 4 hits / 4 total historical comparable major packages
validity_reason: Legislative drafting standards and congressional reporting mechanisms remain stable over multi-year horizons.
